name: Lonestar
caption: GIWF's own first attested World Heavyweight Champion, defending the title in a Gold-belt duster gimmick before losing it in Juarez, Mexico that December.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served Weekly War / PPV show scripts (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).
tenures.note: First attested as champion in the fed's own 26 October 1995 Weekly War; the bout that won him the title is not itself in the held record.

identity.note: Coincidental name match to the held character euwc-lonestar (a different fed, EUWC); no shared evidence.

name: Sal DeFazio
caption: One half of the tag champions Pressure Point, who parlayed a title win over Lonestar in Juarez into a brief singles reign of his own before Theseus Devlin took it from him in January.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served Weekly War / PPV show scripts (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).

name: Gregg "Comet" Matthews
caption: Sal DeFazio's partner in the tag champions Pressure Point, wrestling under a comet-emblazoned gimmick through the fed's Arsenal-vs-Freedom-Brigade era.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served Weekly War / PPV show scripts (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).

name: Theseus Devlin
caption: "The Bod," who took the World Heavyweight title from Sal DeFazio by forcing him to submit in early January 1996.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served title-lineage and rankings snapshots (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).

name: Desert Storm
caption: "The Head Patriot" of the Freedom Brigade, a fatigues-clad World Heavyweight challenger who finally won the title in a ladder match at Wrestle Wrath.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served Weekly War / PPV show scripts (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).

name: Blobber
caption: A Master Mission-managed heavyweight who challenged for the World Title at Wrestle Wrath and lost the ladder match to Desert Storm.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served title-lineage and rankings snapshots (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).

name: Jacob McDonahey
caption: "The I-Man" of the Freedom Brigade, who won the inaugural United States Championship at Turkey Day Titles before losing it to Steve Latini the following April.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served Weekly War / PPV show scripts (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).

identity.note: Coincidental full-name match to the character jacob-mcdonahey-icbinr, named on a different, later fed's own site index (icbinr, 1999); no shared evidence links the two beyond the name.

name: Steve Latini
caption: "The Slasher," managed by Stanley Cupp, who escaped a steel cage ahead of Jacob McDonahey to win the United States Championship at April Showers Showdown.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served Weekly War / PPV show scripts (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).

name: Chaos
caption: A tournament winner who took the inaugural Light-Heavyweight Championship at Turkey Day Titles, aligned with manager Mayhem, before losing the belt to David Stevens that August.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served Weekly War / PPV show scripts (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).

identity.note: "Chaos" is a recurring gimmick name reused by unrelated wrestlers and characters across a dozen different held wings (including the museum's own held giwf wing's own, later, unrelated Chaos). No evidence links this 1995-96 GIWF character to any of them beyond the shared name.

name: David Stevens
caption: "Death Sentence," managed by Christopher Andrews, who beat Wheels for the Light-Heavyweight title in August 1996 and was still defending it successfully as of Gold Rush II that December.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served Weekly War / PPV show scripts (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).

identity.note: Coincidental aka collision with the unit death-sentance-ewa-email (a differently-spelled 'Death Sentance' tag team on a wholly unrelated fed, EWA/E-Mail Wrestling Federation, minted elsewhere in this same accession); no shared evidence.

name: Coach Chris
caption: Winner of the inaugural Women's Championship at Turkey Day Titles, who held the belt for eight months before Mean Man-Mama forced her to submit that July.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served Weekly War / PPV show scripts (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).

name: Mean Man-Mama
caption: Managed by Mr. Burns, she took the Women's Championship from Coach Chris in July 1996 and was still defending it successfully as of Gold Rush II that December.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served title-lineage and rankings snapshots (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).

name: The Narcissist
caption: One-third of Jingoist, who dethroned Pressure Point for the World Tag-Team Championship at Wrestle Wrath.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served title-lineage and rankings snapshots (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).

name: Lt. Liberty
caption: A Freedom Brigade member and one-third of Jingoist, the trio that took the World Tag-Team Championship from Pressure Point at Wrestle Wrath.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served Weekly War / PPV show scripts (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).

name: Major Hawk Hunter
caption: "The Wingman," one-third of Jingoist, the trio that took the World Tag-Team Championship from Pressure Point at Wrestle Wrath.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served title-lineage and rankings snapshots (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).

name: Cyclone
caption: One half of the masked Storm Lords, managed by Christopher Andrews, who fought Pressure Point to a time-limit draw for the World Tag-Team title in October 1995.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served Weekly War / PPV show scripts (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).

identity.note: Coincidental name match to the held character cyclone-apw (a different fed, APW); no shared evidence.

name: Hurricane
caption: One half of the masked Storm Lords, managed by Christopher Andrews, who fought Pressure Point to a time-limit draw for the World Tag-Team title in October 1995.

tenures.source: GIWF's own served Weekly War / PPV show scripts (promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/).

identity.note: Coincidental name match to the held characters hurricane-nfw and hurricane-wicew (unrelated feds); no shared evidence.

name: Janet James
caption: Named the GIWF's own Women's Wrestler of the Year for 1997 at the promotion's Year In Review — she wasn't there to collect it.

tenures.source: the fed's own "2nd Annual Year End Awards and Year In Review" (23 Dec 1997, msg_id 09OHS1j1eu4J); served in part at promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/giwf-weeklywar-1995-yearinreview-1997-12-23.html

name: Nymphet
caption: Voted the GIWF's own Most Annoying wrestler of 1997 in the promotion's Viewer's Choice balloting — the ceremony's hosts sent her off with "good riddance."

tenures.source: the fed's own "2nd Annual Year End Awards and Year In Review" (23 Dec 1997, msg_id 09OHS1j1eu4J); served in part at promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/giwf-weeklywar-1995-yearinreview-1997-12-23.html

name: Wayne Hanson
caption: The GIWF's own 1997 Announcer of the Year — a color commentator who, in an unsanctioned Gold Rush II brawl, stepped from behind the desk to fight as the promotion's own reigning U.S. Heavyweight Champion.

tenures.source: the fed's own "2nd Annual Year End Awards and Year In Review" (23 Dec 1997, msg_ids 09OHS1j1eu4J, rSQSZG-IoFEJ); served in part at promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/giwf-weeklywar-1995-yearinreview-1997-12-23.html

name: "Substance" Chad O'Donnell
caption: Founding member of the Mercenary Enforcement Agency and, with "Bullywug" Glenn Hudson, one half of the GIWF's own 1997 Match of the Year — also honored that year for Outstanding Performance in the Field of Creative Cheating.

tenures.source: the fed's own "2nd Annual Year End Awards and Year In Review" (23 Dec 1997, msg_ids 09OHS1j1eu4J through pz86OAHh9yoJ), whose own retrospective video wall dates a recovered match to 5 April 1996; served in part at promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/giwf-weeklywar-1995-yearinreview-1997-12-23.html

name: "Bullywug" Glenn Hudson
caption: The GIWF's own Best Flasher/Interviewee for 1997 and, with "Substance" Chad O'Donnell, one half of that year's Match of the Year — a member of the Alliance out of Melbourne, Australia.

tenures.source: the fed's own "2nd Annual Year End Awards and Year In Review" (23 Dec 1997, msg_ids 09OHS1j1eu4J through pz86OAHh9yoJ); served in part at promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/giwf-weeklywar-1995-yearinreview-1997-12-23.html

name: K-Solo
caption: Founding member of the Mercenary Enforcement Agency and, with the Violent Librarian, one half of the GIWF's own 1997 Feud of the Year.

caption: A member of the Pickens Army and, with K-Solo, one half of the GIWF's own 1997 Feud of the Year.

name: Brad Vandal
notes: Known also from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 1997: #33, tagged GIWF.
caption: GIWF Heavyweight Champion by his own account, and the promotion's own 1997 Wrestler of the Year, Newcomer of the Year, and Finisher of the Year ("The Vandalizer") — ranked #33 in the RSPWF Top 200 the same year, independent corroboration of the same wrestler.

tenures.source: the fed's own "2nd Annual Year End Awards and Year In Review" (23 Dec 1997, msg_ids 09OHS1j1eu4J, 5cJWypBwAocJ, pz86OAHh9yoJ); served in part at promotions/giwf-weeklywar-1995/archive/giwf-weeklywar-1995-yearinreview-1997-12-23.html

name: Deliverance
notes: Known also from the RSPWF Top 200, the rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy newsgroup's own year-end poll. Placings and the poll's own federation tags, verbatim — 1997: #184, tagged GIWF, the list's own prior-year note reading (#196).
caption: The GIWF's own 1996 Wrestler of the Year and 1997 Best Ring Entrance winner, back the following December to present the award he'd won — ranked #184 in the RSPWF Top 200 the same year, independent corroboration of the same wrestler.
